sections.title: This week's likely biggest movers
sections.markdown:
Amazon and Intel both fell after hours on Oct 29, for different reasons. AWS sped up to 39% while Amazon's cash flow sank further; Intel beat the quarter but guided Q4 far below. For suppliers, the headline is Amazon's plan to spend "meaningfully more" in 2027. Alphabet closed down 12.6%. Next up: Exxon and Chevron (Oct 30), Apple and Palantir (Nov 2), AMD (Nov 3). Each row names the trigger in both directions.

*Updated the evening of Oct 29, after Amazon's and Intel's after-hours reports. After-hours prices are thin and can reverse by the open. This is research, not financial advice; I'm not a licensed advisor, and the buy/sell decision is yours.*

| Stock | Sector | Why it should move most | Upside trigger | Downside trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INTC | AI chips | Down \~17–21% after hours (implied ±9.4%): Q3 beat (EPS $0.52 vs. $0.40, gross margin 44.1%), but Q4 guide of $15B–$16B vs. \~$17.1B expected, 38% margin and $0.25 EPS vs. \~$0.43 | Data center +78% and 18A progress draw dip buyers | Memory costs and wafer limits keep squeezing margins into H1 2027 |
| AMZN | AI cloud | Down \~7% after hours (implied ±7.6%), after closing −4.3%: AWS +39% and a $578B backlog, but EPS $1.89 vs. \~$1.97 and trailing free cash flow −$42.4B | Buyers reward AWS speeding up and the >40% growth target for 2027–28 | Cash-burn selling that took GOOGL down 12.6% repeats |
| MU, SKHY, AVGO, MRVL | AI chips and memory | Amazon will spend "meaningfully more" in 2027; Trainium commitments up 20x+; Intel blamed memory costs, a pricing signal for MU and SKHY; MRVL fell 13% Oct 29 on Lumentum deal talks | Suppliers trade on rising capex, not hyperscaler cash flow | "Capex peak" or funding-stress talk; memory is a crowded trade |
| VRT, GEV | AI infrastructure | Amazon's Q3 capex was $77.3B (vs. $35.1B a year ago) and 2027 goes higher | Amazon's 2027 signal outweighs Microsoft's under-spend | Profit-taking after VRT's 16–17% jump on Oct 28 |
| AMD, AAPL | AI chips, hardware | Intel sees its PC unit down >20% next quarter on memory costs; AMD reports Nov 3 (implied ±8.9%), Apple Nov 2 (±4.3%) | AMD takes server share while Intel is supply-limited | The same memory squeeze hits AMD's PC chips and Apple's margins |
| CRWV, NBIS, ORCL | AI cloud (neoclouds) | AWS's backlog says demand still outruns capacity, but a December hike is \~84% priced with the 10-year near 4.96–4.99% | Yields keep easing; Amazon confirms capacity shortage | Hike odds climb; cash-burn fear spreads to debt-funded builders |
| NOW, PLTR | AI software | NOW fell >20% Oct 29 on its soft Q4 guide; PLTR reports Nov 2 (implied ±11.7%) | A strong PLTR guide separates AI winners from seat-based SaaS | Software-wide derating spreads |

sections.title: Macro backdrop: a hawkish hold, 5% yields and $100+ oil
sections.markdown:
The Fed held, but two votes for a hike keep a December 9 increase the market's base case, which keeps pressure on high-multiple and debt-funded AI stocks.

**Oct 29 update:** Q3 GDP grew 3.4% annualized (vs. 3.2% expected) and September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% (core 3.1%, in line); jobless claims were 194,000. The 10-year eased to about 4.96–4.99%, but futures still price \~84% odds of a December 9 hike. The Nasdaq fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.3% to \~7,720 on Alphabet's drop, while small caps rose \~1%. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-29-2026), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

- Fed: held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike. The statement said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine" the stance and called uncertainty elevated. Warsh would not commit to December and said he won't decide meetings in advance. Futures price roughly 83–85% odds of a December hike. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fed-chair-warsh-hesitates-on-december-rate-hike-amid-rising-treasury-yields), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))
- Inflation: September CPI rose 3.7% (core 2.6%), up from 3.4% in August. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html))
- Rates: the 10-year rose about 5 bp to \~5.04% during the press conference while the 2-year fell to 4.70%. A steeper curve hurts long-duration growth stocks and debt-funded builders most. ([SRN News](https://srnnews.com/fomc-holds-rates-steady-markets-rise-modestly/))
- Stocks: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98 and the chip index (SOX) 1.8%, its fourth straight gain. Utilities and real estate lagged on higher long yields. After hours, QQQ slipped \~0.5% on Alphabet. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))
- Oil: Brent near $111 and WTI near $101. Iran's reply to Qatar's new draft deal is expected by week's end. ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/))
- AI financing: Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (−$9.1B). It raised $12.4B from share sales and $28.7B in debt during the quarter. ([Cautious Optimism](https://www.cautiousoptimism.news/msft-alpha-earnings), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative))

sections.title: Options timing: are earnings options cheap or expensive?
sections.markdown:
Intel moved about twice its implied move; Amazon landed just inside its own. Three of this week's five big reports (Alphabet, ServiceNow, Intel) blew through what options priced, each on guidance or cash flow rather than the headline beat. Buying calls or puts into a report only pays if the stock moves more than options already price in. Implied moves for upcoming reports are as of Oct 28 and will shift.

| Stock | Report | Implied move | Actual, or avg. last 5 (close) | Beat implied, last 5 (close) | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INTC | Oct 29 (done) | ±9.4% | −17.6% to −21% after hours | 3 of 5 before tonight | Beat implied, about 2x, to the downside on the Q4 guide |
| AMZN | Oct 29 (done) | ±7.6% | \~−7% after hours (after −4.3% in the day session) | 3 of 5 before tonight | Just inside implied; the pre-report slide took some of the move |
| GOOGL | Oct 28 (done) | ±6.1% | −12.6% close Oct 29 | 2 of 5 before | Twice the implied move; after hours understated it |
| NOW | Oct 28 (done) | ±10.4% | Down >20% on Oct 29 | — | Twice the implied move, to the downside |
| MSFT | Oct 28 (done) | ±4.7%–5.3% | +2% to +6% after hours, roughly flat to −2% on Oct 29 | 3 of 5 before | Inside implied; gains faded |
| PLTR | Nov 2, after close | ±11.7% | ±11.8% | 1 of 5 | Fairly priced; one +29.5% outlier in August |
| AAPL | Nov 2, after close | ±4.3% | ±2.8% | 1 of 5 | Rich vs. recent moves; one −7.4% miss in July |
| AMD | Nov 3, after close | ±8.9% | ±10.4% | 2 of 5 | Slightly cheap on average; two big moves (+18.6%, −17.3%) |
| NVDA | Late Nov. (unconfirmed) | Not priced yet (last ±5.9%) | ±4.0% | 1 of 5 | Options have overpriced the closing move 4 of the last 5 times |

**What this means for timing:**

1. After hours is not the close. Alphabet's −8% to −10% after hours became −12.6% at the close, while Microsoft's gain faded to roughly flat. Amazon's and Intel's moves can widen or narrow by Friday's open; the averages above use closing moves.
2. This week's lesson: when a report changes the cash-flow or guidance story, options history understates the move. Alphabet, ServiceNow and Intel all beat on headline numbers and still fell about twice their implied moves. History is a base rate, not a forecast.
3. Fair or rich options (AAPL, PLTR, NVDA): buying calls or puts outright before the report has had poor odds. Debit spreads cut the cost; waiting until after the report avoids the volatility crush but misses the gap.
4. Cheaper options (AMD): moves have beaten the implied move more often, but on five reports with two outliers. Intel's PC warning adds a new risk to AMD's client business.
5. Read-through stocks (MU, SKHY, AVGO, MRVL, VRT, CRWV, NBIS): no earnings premium of their own to collapse, so a hyperscaler report reprices them overnight. Amazon tonight is the latest such event; Nvidia in late November is the next big one.
6. Expiries: the first weekly after a report (Nov 6 for AAPL, PLTR and AMD) is cheapest but takes the full crush. One more week adds cushion.

Past moves don't predict the next one. Sources: [EarningsWatcher MSFT](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/msft-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher GOOGL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/googl-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMZN](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher AMZN options](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amzn-earnings-options), [EarningsWatcher INTC](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/intc-earnings-october-2026), [EarningsWatcher AAPL](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/aapl-implied-move), [EarningsWatcher PLTR](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/pltr-earnings-november-2026), [EarningsWatcher AMD](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/amd-earnings-november-2026), [Q3 implied vs. actual tracker](https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/q3-2026-implied-vs-actual-tracker), [ZeroHedge (MSFT after hours)](https://zerohedge.com/markets/msft-rises-azure-beat-bookings-shrink-and-backlog-stalls), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower), [Investing.com (GOOGL)](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-alphabet-q3-2026-profit-miss-sparks-10-afterhours-drop-93CH-5662008), [PANews (NOW)](https://panews.io/articles/01a1844b-23c0-762e-84fc-a5ee2a94208b), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours).

sections.title: AI cloud
sections.markdown:
Amazon confirmed the pattern: the market pays for cloud growth but sells negative free cash flow. AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years, yet the stock fell \~7% after hours because trailing free cash flow hit −$42.4B and 2027 capex goes higher still. Alphabet closed down 12.6% on the same worry.

| Company | Result or setup | Versus the bar | Read |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Amazon (AMZN), Q3 2026](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx) | Revenue $201.9B (+12%) vs. \~$202.2B; EPS $1.89 vs. \~$1.97; AWS $46.0B (+39%), 38.7% margin; record 13.9% company operating margin | Backlog $578B; Q3 capex $77.3B; 2026 held at \~$220B, 2027 "meaningfully more"; trailing free cash flow −$42.4B; Q4 sales guide $240B–$247B | Down \~7% after hours (implied ±7.6%); AWS seen growing >40% in 2027 and 2028 |
| [Microsoft (MSFT)](https://phemex.com/news/article/microsoft-q1-fy2027-revenue-hits-923b-as-azure-grows-48-yoy-101615), fiscal Q1 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) | Revenue $92.3B (+19%), EPS $4.89; Azure +48% cc vs. 44–45% guide; Microsoft Cloud $63.9B (+30%) | Capex incl. leases $45.2B vs. \~$50B+ expected; commercial bookings −12%; RPO flat at $677B; FQ2 Azure guide reported at \~49% | Up 2–6% after hours, then roughly flat to −2% on Oct 29 |
| [Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative), Q3 2026 | Revenue $127.6B (+25%) vs. \~$128.2B; EPS $2.12 vs. \~$3.02 (an $8.7B investment loss cut $0.55); Cloud $30.7B (+103%), 36.2% margin | Backlog $561B (from $514B); capex $51.4B; 2026 guide held at $195B–$205B; 2027 to "rise significantly"; free cash flow −$9.1B | Closed −12.6% Oct 29, about $500B of market value |
| Meta (META, reported Oct 21) | Revenue +26% to $64.6B; free cash flow −$2.1B | 2026 capex now $135B–$145B | New non-voting class to fund AI shows how capital-hungry this is |
| Oracle, CoreWeave, Nebius | ORCL +10.7% Oct 28 on investor day: >35% yearly revenue growth FY26–FY30, ≥$225B FY30 revenue; CRWV +7.3%, NBIS +7.0% | Funding costs with the 10-year near 5%; CRWV bonds near 15% | The leveraged tail; moves 2–3x the hyperscalers on any news |

**Most likely to move:** Amazon at Friday's open, then CoreWeave and Nebius. Amazon now needs to show its AWS acceleration can outrun its spending; the >40% growth target for 2027–28 is the bull case, cash burn the bear case. For the neoclouds, a $578B AWS backlog says demand still exceeds capacity, which supports their order books; but they remain most exposed to cash-burn fears and a December hike.

**Second-order effect:** Alphabet said TPU system sales were a meaningful part of Cloud growth and expects a bigger ramp in 2027, making Google a chip seller as well as a cloud. OpenAI and Oracle are reported to be using Google's chips. **Disclosure:** Anthropic, the company that makes me, is a large Google TPU customer, so weigh my framing here.

**Amazon second-order effects:** Trainium and Graviton revenue commitments each rose more than 20x, most Bedrock workloads run on Trainium, and Amazon plans to sell Trainium to outside customers starting late 2027. That makes Amazon, like Google, a chip seller as well as a cloud, a long-run threat to Nvidia's share and a tailwind for memory makers. **Disclosure:** Amazon is a major investor in Anthropic, the company that makes me, and Anthropic is a large AWS and Trainium customer; Amazon's EPS decline was partly a tough comparison with Anthropic investment gains a year ago. Weigh my framing here accordingly.

sections.title: AI infrastructure: power and cooling
sections.markdown:
The "picks and shovels" suppliers both reported blowout quarters this morning. They are the cleanest read on what hyperscaler capex turns into.

| Company | Q3 2026 result | What it tells us |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertiv (VRT) | Sales $4.31B (+61%) vs. \~$3.75B expected; adj. EPS $2.21 vs. $1.82; organic orders up over 100%; raised full-year guidance | Power and cooling demand is accelerating, not peaking; stock was up \~4% early today |
| GE Vernova (GEV) | Orders $29B (+96% organic); backlog $197B; buyback raised to $20B | Gas turbines for data centers are sold out years ahead; expects 130+ GW under contract by year-end |
| SLB | Revenue $9.45B; highlighted Data Center Solutions as a separate growth driver | Even oil-services firms are selling into the AI power build |

**Most likely to move:** Vertiv, again. Amazon spent $77.3B on capex in Q3, more than double a year ago, and said 2027 will be "meaningfully more" than this year's \~$220B, while describing AWS as still short of capacity. That offsets Microsoft's under-spend and supports Vertiv's order book after its 16–17% jump on Oct 28; the risk is profit-taking if the cash-burn selloff in hyperscalers spreads. GE Vernova, with a backlog contracted out to about 2031, stays the steadier way the market expresses the same power demand. ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-29-amazoncom-inc-stock/), [Amazon Q3 release](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-28-2026), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))

**Risk:** GE Vernova fell more than 14% in the month before earnings as investors worried about how AI gets financed. A capex pause from any hyperscaler hits this group fast.

Sources: [Vertiv Q3 release (TradingView)](https://www.tradingview.com/news/prnewswire:4c4865b67a1a7:0-vertiv-reports-strong-third-quarter-2026-with-net-sales-growth-of-61-organic-orders-growth-over-100-and-diluted-eps-growth-of-91-adjusted-diluted-eps-growth-of-78-raises-full-year-2026-guidance-across-all-key-metrics/), [MarketBeat (VRT)](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/VRT/earnings/), [Yahoo (VRT)](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/VRT/), [GE Vernova 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001996810/000199681026000162/gevpressrelease3q26.htm), [247 Wall St (GEV)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/24/the-ai-power-bill-comes-due-will-ge-vernovas-q3-earnings-oct-28-prove-its-176b-backlog-is-real/), [SLB release](https://www.benzinga.com/node/62553977).

sections.title: AI chips and memory
sections.markdown:
Amazon is the new demand signal: Q3 capex of $77.3B, 2027 "meaningfully more," and Trainium commitments up more than 20x. Intel added a second one: memory costs are now squeezing chip buyers, which is pricing power for memory makers. Chips still fell on Oct 29 (semiconductor ETF down \~2%, Micron and Arm down 3%+, Broadcom −1.9%, Nvidia −0.8%) as Alphabet's drop and weak Korean memory results weighed. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Intel (INTC)](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/intel-q3-2026-slides-record-data-center-growth-stock-tumbles-on-outlook-93CH-4985517) | Q3 revenue $16.5B (+21%); data center $7.3B (+78%); foundry loss $1.9B (margin −27.7% from −36.2%), outside foundry revenue $411M; Q4 guide $15B–$16B at 38% margin; down \~17–21% after hours | Data center strength is real, but memory costs, a Fab 28 shutdown (\~$300M, \~200 bp of margin), supply limits into H1 2027 and no positive free cash flow in 2027 dominate |
| Micron (MU) | Says 2027 HBM is largely sold out at "much higher" prices; DRAM prices rose high-teens % last quarter, NAND \~30%; down 3%+ Oct 29 | Amazon's 2027 capex raise and Intel's memory-cost warning both point to more pricing power |
| SK Hynix (SKHY, Nasdaq ADR) | Record Q3; says DRAM and HBM sold out through 2029; up \~13% on Oct 28 | Same thesis; TrendForce sees DRAM contract prices up another 10–15% in Q4 |
| Marvell (MRVL) | Fell 13.2% to $218.34 on Oct 29 on reported advanced talks to buy Lumentum (LITE) in an all-stock deal; an announcement could come next week | Dilution and integration risk vs. owning more of the AI optics chain; also a custom-chip supplier to Amazon |
| Broadcom (AVGO) | Banks lining up a \~$63B financing to build AI compute (with Apollo, Blackstone); −1.9% Oct 29 | Custom chips for AI labs, including Google's TPUs; Alphabet says TPU system sales ramp into 2027 |
| TSMC (TSM) | Q3 revenue $46.7B, above the top of guidance; net income +68.7% | Makes Trainium, TPUs and Nvidia GPUs alike, so every capex raise lands here; margin dilution from 2 nm and U.S. fabs is the drag |
| AMD | Reports Nov 3; guided $12.7B–$13.3B; implied ±8.9% | Intel's supply limits are a server share opportunity; Intel's PC warning is a risk to AMD's client unit |
| Nvidia (NVDA) | Reports late Nov. (unconfirmed); −0.8% Oct 29 | Amazon and Google now both sell their own AI chips; Nvidia's report is the AI-cycle verdict |

**Most likely to move:** Intel at Friday's open (down \~17–21% after hours, about twice its implied move). Then Micron and SK Hynix on Amazon's 2027 capex and Intel's memory-cost warning, Marvell on Lumentum deal news, and AMD into its Nov 3 report. Nvidia faces a growing custom-chip story, now from both Google and Amazon, until its own report in late November.

**Risk:** Memory was the most crowded trade in the October selloff. SK Hynix fell 9.6% in one session during that slide, so the downside is just as sharp.

**Disclosure:** Some Broadcom financing reporting ties these deals to Anthropic, the company that makes me. I note it so you can weigh my framing.

Sources: [Tech Insider (Micron)](https://tech-insider.org/micron-ceo-2027-memory-supply-sold-out-2026/), [Computing for Geeks (TrendForce)](https://computingforgeeks.com/?p=175309), [Yahoo live blog](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html), [NordFX](https://nordfx.com/market-news/market-pulse-october-28-2026), [TSMC 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000726/a3q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm), [AllInvestView (TSMC)](https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/2330.TW/q3-2026/), [Yahoo (Broadcom)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html), [247 Wall St (Intel)](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/25/intels-make-or-break-margin-test-is-arriving-on-oct-29/), [Benzinga (AMD)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/amd/earnings-forecasts), [The Right Trader (NVDA)](https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/nvda), [FX Leaders](https://www.fxleaders.com/?p=465067).

sections.title: AI software
sections.markdown:
ServiceNow's after-hours drop shows the AI-disruption trade against seat-based software is not over, even when growth and AI bookings beat. Companies selling AI outcomes still rerate up; legacy SaaS trades on fear that AI agents replace it.

| Company | Setup | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Palantir (PLTR) | Reports Nov 2; est. $0.36 EPS, $2.00B revenue; beat 5 straight quarters | Highest-multiple AI software name; guidance decides the reaction |
| ServiceNow (NOW) | Q3 subscription revenue $3.99B (+21%, +20.5% cc) vs. \~20% guide; AI contract-value target raised to $1.7B from $1B; EPS $1.00 vs. $1.02; Q4 guide below the Street; fell more than 20% on Oct 29 | Disruption fear won again despite beats on growth and AI |
| Microsoft (MSFT) | Copilot adoption and its own models, alongside Azure | The software side of tonight's report |
**Most likely to move:** Palantir on Nov 2 (implied ±11.7%). ServiceNow's 20%+ drop on Oct 29, with Fortinet, Atlassian and Workday also down 6–20%, shows only accelerating growth with a strong guide is being rewarded. Amazon's Bedrock data cuts the other way for AI-native software: Fortune 500 spending on Bedrock rose nearly 7x and agent deployments doubled. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [Amazon Q3 release](https://ir.aboutamazon.com/news-release/news-release-details/2026/Amazon-com-Announces-Third-Quarter-Results/default.aspx), [Securities.io](https://www.securities.io/servicenow-q3-subscription-revenue-rises-21-to-3-988-million/), [PANews](https://panews.io/articles/01a1844b-23c0-762e-84fc-a5ee2a94208b))

**Sector event:** Anthropic has filed an S-1 to list on Nasdaq. A large AI listing can pull money from existing AI software stocks, or reprice them higher as a comparison point.

**Disclosure:** I'm built by Anthropic, so I'm not a neutral source on that IPO. I won't give a view on it; treat it purely as a sector catalyst.

Sources: [Benzinga (PLTR)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLTR/earnings), [Earnings Whispers (PLTR drift)](https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PLTR), [XTB (NOW)](https://www.xtb.com/cy/market-analysis/news-and-research/servicenow-shares-jump-7-after-earnings-is-the-software-sector-poised-for-a-rebound), [TIKR (NOW)](https://www.tikr.com/blog/servicenow-jumped-7-on-a-150-analyst-target-heres-where-the-stock-could-go), [Yahoo market wrap](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-oct-28-081900420.html).

sections.title: Oil and gas
sections.markdown:
Earnings are huge, but the stocks now trade on one binary question: does the Iran conflict end? A deal would cut the war premium quickly; refiners carry the most exposure.

| Company | Latest data point | Why it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Valero (VLO) | Q3 adj. EPS $23.90 vs. $20.30 expected; refining margin $39.24/bbl vs. $13.14 a year ago | Most leveraged to war-driven fuel margins, both ways |
| Exxon (XOM), Chevron (CVX) | Report Oct 30; Exxon flagged a $4.5B refining-margin boost; CVX est. $4.78 | Steadier; buybacks and Guyana/Permian growth cushion a price drop |
| SLB | Revenue $9.45B (+6%); Middle East up 13% sequentially despite disruption | Services lag the oil price; growing data center unit |

**Most likely to move:** Refiners (VLO, and Phillips 66 reporting about Nov 4). Iran's reply to the Qatari draft is due by week's end. President Trump has said he expects the war to end after the Nov 3 midterms, with oil falling. In August, the EIA forecast Brent at $69 in 2027 once Hormuz traffic normalizes.

**Upside case:** New supply shocks keep happening; a Saudi refinery was attacked this week and pushed oil higher.

Sources: [Oilprice (Valero)](https://oilprice.com/Company-News/Valero-Q3-Earnings-Surge-Sixfold-to-68-Billion-on-Refining-Boom.amp.html), [247 Wall St (Valero)](https://247wallst.com/cards/valero-energy-q3-2026-earnings-vlo-01m5hs2e7dnht5h4w2ey4hf68p), [Pluang (Exxon, Trump)](https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/trump-perkirakan-perang-iran-berakhir-harga-minyak-turun-setelah-pemilu), [SLB release](https://www.sttinfo.fi/tiedote/72439583/slb-announces-third-quarter-2026-results?publisherId=58763726), [AInvest (EIA)](https://www.ainvest.com/news/iran-oil-windfall-priced-eia-won-2608/), [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/), [Yahoo live blog](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-october-28-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fed-meeting-decision-big-tech-earnings-130508769.html).

sections.title: Scenarios: what would change the picture
sections.markdown:
| If this happens | Likely winners | Likely losers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hyperscalers raise capex and cloud growth accelerates | MU, SKHY, VRT, GEV, AVGO, CRWV | Hyperscaler stocks themselves if cash flow weakens |
| Capex rises but cloud growth slows | Suppliers short-term | GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN (repeat of Alphabet's July drop) |
| Fed signals a December hike | Banks, cash | CRWV, NBIS, ORCL, high-multiple software |
| Fed sounds patient, yields ease below 5% | Leveraged AI builders, small caps | — |
| Iran deal reached | Airlines, consumers | VLO, XOM, CVX, oil services |
| Iran talks collapse | VLO, XOM, CVX | Rate-sensitive tech (oil feeds inflation, inflation feeds hikes) |

Oct 29 played out the first row for both sides: Amazon raised its 2027 spending signal and AWS sped up (good for MU, SKHY, VRT, GEV), while its stock fell on cash flow, the "hyperscaler stocks themselves" loser. Intel added a new risk not in this table: memory costs squeezing chip buyers and PC makers (AMD client, Apple).
